method.rerun: S1 to S5 had no JSON (empty or missing in the earlier pass); re-run on 26 Oct 2026, each exit 0, stderr empty. S6 and S7 were kept.
method.record_check: recgrep.py (earlier) and tight.py (this pass: narrower regexes, front matter only)
method.verification: verify.py (earlier agent and this pass) plus hand checks of every MISMATCH against the vendored line
method.layers: RENDERED (R*: honest_limit or guard only), LOADED, IDENTIFIED (kept in each cell's identified list, not a table code), OTHER, NOTHING

sub_questions.label: Was wealth a sin; the rich young man; the camel; prosperity teaching
Giving: tithe, alms, almsgiving and forgiveness
Sharing in common as in Acts
Care for the poor, widows, orphans, the sick, non-Christians
Who paid for churches and bishops; accounts, corruption, taking from the poor, paying to belong
Work and class: jobs a Christian could not do, who the members were, who paid for the way of life

canon_demonstrations._note: Counted from records/*/demonstration front matter (canon_cells, canon_question_id); the cell-tag counts on other record types are in cell_tags.

S1.note: Clement, Quis dives 16 (tagged F5-T, F4-T): possessions as gifts, master not slave; not_for forbids "must give everything away". Verified. The camel/rich-young-man text itself is the same treatise, unquoted.

S2.note: Only a guard: not_for bars a fixed tithe. No record on alms and forgiveness; anf02 33748 (Clement: law forbids a brother usury, "open hands") and 15 alms hits are unread for this.

source_hits.snippet: held in common x2, distribution was made

S3.note: No record. Clementine Homilies and Eusebius carry Acts 4 language (anf08, npnf201 held in common x2); not read in context for Alexandria.

S4.note: The sick, nursed through the plague of c.260 (Eusebius VII.22, verified). Widows, orphans and non-Christians are not covered; not_for bars reading it as a charity programme.

source_hits.snippet: the law prohibits a brother from taking usury

S5.note: No record. Clement, Strom. (anf02 33748) and Nicaea canon 17 (npnf214 5000) hold the usury rule; Apocalypse of Peter (anf09 10863) puts usurers in hell.

S6.note: No record on money. Eusebius VI.3: Origen took four oboli a day from the buyer of his manuscripts (npnf201 32818).

S7.note: Record gap: alx.term.oikos and quote.timothy-ordinary-questions (F5-I) do not reach work or class. Origen selling manuscripts (npnf201 32818) is the only trade evidence found.

S1.note: Strongest world; witness tagged F5-T. No quote record: the records call the homilies "unverified", but npnf208 5069-5284, 6236-6290 and 6926 carry English extracts (Hom. on Ps. 14, Hom. VI on Luke 12, Hom. VIII), including "Do not wait for a famine before thou openest thy barns" (6272).

S2.note: Almsgiving as love of the poor, doctrine inside it. No tithe or almsgiving-and-forgiveness record.

S3.note: Basil, Longer Rules VII, verified (OCR footnote mark and "Tor" only). Brotherhood goods in common; not Acts at large.

S4.note: Poorhouse, leper-house, famine relief; the complex is text-attested only, and the records say so.

S5.note: Usury preached against in famine. Same gap as S1: the words are in npnf208 5069-5284 (Hom. on Ps. 14: "the borrower bends to necessity and is beaten"), Nicaea c.17 (npnf214 5000) and Clarke 5904, but no quote record.

S6.note: Bishop as public patron, church property held in trust, governors negotiated for the complex. Account-keeping and corruption not covered.

S7.note: Work and prayer (Longer Rules XXXVII, verified, OCR glyphs only); learned instrument against "fishermen"; Nyssa on slavery. Lay trades and class of members not covered.

S1.note: Rich-young-man call is the founding story; four quotes verified. Three-hundred-acres is tagged Contested (alternate reading made it a tax transaction).

S2.note: F4-T limit says no source names a tithe, "checked" in the Vita and Palladius only. Cassian, Conference XXI (npnf211 44550-44680, mapped to desert) discusses tithes and first-fruits and how renouncers go beyond them. The limit is wider than its check.

S3.note: Pachomian koinonia, scoped to the federation; not Acts 2 or the solitary strand. Quote verified.

S4.note: Giving to the poor only as the monk's own renunciation. No record on widows, orphans, sick or outsiders; the Sayings are not mined.

S5.note: No record. Little in Cassian (npnf211, 4 lines) and nothing from the Sayings or Palladius.

S6.note: Contested gravity (tagged F5-T, F5-I): settlements traded and took alms; Kellia and the Nepheros dossier. Not the question of who paid for bishops.

S7.note: Best-covered cell in the fleet for work (tagged F5-T and F5-I). Unrendered: Palladius ch. XXXII at Panopolis (clarke1918 line 405): 15 tailors, 7 smiths, 4 carpenters, 15 fullers, and the tablet list of trades.

S1.note: F5-T witness names one rich member (Lucilla, 400 pieces, Gesta apud Zenophilum 320); not_for bars any claim on Donatist teaching on wealth.

S2.note: F4-T witness retrieves on tithing, then not_for bars any claim about it. A guard, not an answer.

S3.note: No record. Only hostile or Catholic voices (Augustine, npnf104 4620).

S4.note: Only "goods of the poor" as a charge of theft; no record of Donatist relief.

S5.note: No record. Optatus III.4 (optatus_against-the-donatists.txt 2002): Axido and Fasir's men made "acknowledgments of indebtedness" worthless. Hostile, and the Circumcellion records do not use it.

S6.note: The 320 inquiry into church silver is the most documentary money story in the fleet (Documented).

S7.note: Honest limit on work and daily life; Circumcellion class is Dominant Modern Reconstruction, Numidia only.

S1.note: Cassian's renunciation and Salvian's "rich murdering the poor"; verified (Salvian 5063-5066 after a false mismatch from line breaks).

S2.note: No record. Cassian, Conference XXI (npnf211 44596-44680) on tithes and first-fruits; Augustine anti-Pelagian alms (npnf105).

S3.note: Cenobitic goods "consecrated to the Lord"; Cassian's East, not a Gallic house.

S4.note: Beggar at Amiens and the guest as Christ; verified. Cloak scene tagged Contested.

S5.note: No record. Cassian (npnf211 7716, 39549-39556) repeats the usury ban; Cyprian, De lapsis on bishops "multiplying usuries" (anf05 43784).

S6.note: Tax and Salvian's curials, not church funding. Nothing on who paid for bishops.

S7.note: The one clear "job a Christian left": Martin's discharge. Verified. Craft and farm work are not covered.

S1.note: Paula's divestment is a contested_claim (totality unchecked); the aristocratic base is plain. Jerome's camel and Mammon passages (npnf206, 20 and 16 hits) are unquoted.

S2.note: "We did not tithe": giving was directional and total. Absence stated inside a witness, not a limit record. Jerome says he "lives on the tithe" (npnf206 11331).

S3.note: No record. Jerome and Cassian on Acts 4 (npnf206 22 hits, npnf211).

S4.note: Fabiola's hospital and the Portus hostel; both quotes verified; the "first hospital" claim is flagged uncorroborated.

S5.note: No record. Jerome on the talents "with usury" (npnf206 4902, 39602) and Letter on clergy (npnf203 13588).

S6.note: Patronage stood where office stands elsewhere; not_for bars presenting Jerome's account as independently confirmed.

S7.note: Who the members were: senatorial women and a scholar. The "educated rich" charge (C10-05) is answered by implication; no record on ordinary members or trades.

S1.note: F5-T limit: money seen "from above". Ammianus on Roman bishops' luxury is an outsider (verified; OCR repairs only).

S2.note: Leo's collections, proportional, no fixed tenth (Documented, tagged F4-T).

S3.note: No record. Chrysostom, Hom. Acts (npnf111 5850, 65 Ananias hits).

S4.note: Collections for ransom, strangers, the poor. No hospital or widow record; Ambrose on ransoming captives (npnf210) unquoted.

S5.note: No record. Leo, Letter 4 c.4: usury forbidden to clergy and laity (npnf212 1549); Nicaea c.17.

S6.note: Emperor-built basilicas and imperial wealth flowing into the church; Theodosian Code XVI is vendored.

S7.note: Honest limits only; courts and bishops noticed ordinary people only in crowds.

S1.note: F5-T witness (status draft): "Some among us were rich", Cyprian to a rich matron. Draft; compiled-package state unchecked.

S2.note: Cyprian, On Works and Alms: almsgiving as the remedy for post-baptismal sin. Draft. Tithe: Augustine Sermon on the Mount (npnf106 17294) unquoted.

S3.note: No record. Augustine (npnf103 42112; npnf104 4620; npnf106 13584) on Acts 4; Cyprian, Unity ch. 25.

S4.note: Ransom of captives and plague; both draft.

S5.note: No record. Cyprian, De lapsis: bishops "multiplied usuries" (anf05 43784); Testimonia III.48 "we must not take usury" (52955); Augustine on Ps. 37 and sermons.

S6.note: No record. Cyprian on monthly division and stipends (anf05 31392, 32283); Benson 19625 on the sportula.

S7.note: No record. Augustine, City of God on actors and trades (npnf102, 35 lines); Benson on gladiators.

S1.note: F5-T witness: Hermas, Sim. 2, elm and vine, rich and poor needed; not_for: teaching, not practice.

S2.note: No record. Polycarp 10 "alms delivers from death" (anf01 3512); Didache 4, 13 in anf07; Two Ways story only mentions alms instruction.

S3.note: Lucian: all brothers, property held in common (verified); hostile outsider. Didache 4.8 "share all" in the story, Inferential-Thin.

S4.note: Widows, orphans, prisoners, collection at Justin's Sunday gathering; Lucian verified.

S5.note: No record. Tertullian, Against Marcion IV.17 on loans and usury (anf03 31326); Hermas and Clement (anf02 20980).

S6.note: No record on who paid. Didache on supporting prophets is in anf07; the prisoner story has leaders bribing jailers.

S7.note: Limits only. Tertullian, De idololatria (anf03 4968-6200: artificers, schoolmasters at 5484, military service at 6145) is vendored and mapped here, and unrendered.

S1.note: F5-T limit says no record addresses wealth teaching "as such". True of records; the library holds Calvin, Institutes (vol. 2 12530) and Zwingli on the rich (vol. 3 14689).

S2.note: No record; rzg.witness.why-the-children-too says tithing is not claimed. Zwingli on tithes (vol. 1 5372, 7911; vol. 3 12173; editor or Zwingli not traced); Calvin, Institutes (vol. 3 12547).

S3.note: No record. Zwingli, Selected Works 5519, 6368, 6847: Anabaptists "hold all things in common"; his answer.

S4.note: No record. Calvin, Institutes (vol. 3 2436, deacons and care of the poor); Quick, Synodicon (Reformed France). The 1541 Ordinances are registered, unvendored.

S5.note: No record. Zwingli, Latin Works vol. 3 (5478, 5487, 7334: "putteth not out his money to usury"); Quick 15235 "All Usury".

S6.note: No record. Quick, Synodicon (stipends, common stock); ministers' pay in the 1541 Ordinances (unvendored).

S1.note: Ephrem rebukes the rich of Edessa in the famine (Widely Accepted; not eyewitness).

S2.note: No record. Aphrahat, Dem. VII (hallock 44): "alms are given to the poor, and the rich have no need"; Apostolic Constitutions tithes (anf07, 8 hits). Alms hits in npnf213 are Gregory the Great.

S3.note: No record. Qyama records mention communal life only; no Acts text read.

S4.note: Famine relief and the hospitaller; Aphrahat Dem. VI "visit our Lord in the persons of the sick". Three quotes verified.

S5.note: No record. Ephrem, Nisibene (npnf213 17672, usurers watching by night) is the only Syriac hit; the Basil and Nicaea hits are other worlds' texts.

S6.note: The rich "trusted no one to handle the giving honestly"; Ephrem appoints himself hospitaller. The only accounts-and-trust story in the fleet.

S7.note: Limit on enslaved members only. Nothing on trades or class.

S1.note: F5-T witness and quote (Large Catechism, 7th commandment; verified); not_for: no claim that wealth is condemned or anyone named rich.

S2.note: F4-T witness retrieves on tithing, then not_for says records do not show it. Good works include alms.

S3.note: No record. Apology of the Augsburg Confession (melanchthon 7025): monks called "community of property" evangelical; Luther vol. 2 on the sacrament.

S4.note: Do not turn the poor man away (verified). No record on the common chest or relief organisation.

S5.note: No record. Luther vol. 1 6560 (usurious sale of rents) and a "Of Usury" contents line (6314); Table Talk 2948. "Trade and Usury" is not vendored.

S6.note: No record. Luther v1 14853, 14963 on tithes and annates; Saxon visitation protocols registered, unvendored.

S7.note: Calling and office: "every trade has its own office"; F5-I-tagged. Doctrine of station, not a record of what members did.

findings: Cappadocian: records say the Basil homilies are unverified, but npnf208 5069-5284, 6236-6290, 6926 hold English extracts; no quote record exists for S1, S4 or S5.

No world has a demonstration for money (F5-T), tithe (F4-T) or work (F5-I); usury has records in one world of twelve.
